hook.line: Everything the doctor tells Hernando is also true for everyone else: drink water, skip the salt, no smoking in the waiting room. When advice is for anybody, Spanish has a few short ways to say it without naming a person.
hook.en: You need to drink lots of water.

examples.en: You need to drink lots of water.
There's no need to be afraid.

rule:
When a rule or piece of advice is for anybody, you don't name a person. Three ways to start, and a fourth coming soon:

*Hay que* + infinitive: you need to, one must. *Hay que tomar agua*.
*Se debe* + infinitive: it should be done. *No se debe fumar aquí*.
*Uno tiene que* + infinitive: you have to, as people do. *Uno tiene que comer bien*.
*Conviene* + infinitive: it's a good idea. You will see it soon, and it works the same way.

Watch the *no*. *No se debe fumar* says you must not. *No hay que fumar* says you don't need to. Spanish uses *uno* for the general "you", where English also says "one" or "you".
smallPrint: Teachers call these impersonal constructions of obligation: no subject is named, so the rule applies to everyone.

options: I drink a lot of water.
You need to drink a lot of water.
They drink a lot of water.
You don't have to smoke here.
There's no need to smoke here.
You have to eat well, as anyone does.

readAndPick.es: No se debe comer tanta sal.
options: You shouldn't eat so much salt.
You don't need to eat so much salt.
One needs to eat less salt.
There's no need to be afraid.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right form and type the whole sentence: *___ tomar mucha agua.* (*Hay que* or *Uno nunca*) You need to drink lots of water.
yourTurn.why: A need that applies to anyone is *hay que* plus an infinitive.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right form and type the whole sentence: *No ___ fumar aquí.* (*se debe* or *hay que*) Smoking isn't allowed here.
yourTurn.why: A ban is *no se debe*; *no hay que* would mean you don't need to.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: You never know.
Type in Spanish: You should rest a little.
yourTurn.why: *Se debe* plus an infinitive says what should be done.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it a ban: *Hay que fumar aquí.* Say that smoking isn't allowed here.
yourTurn.why: *No se debe* is the way to say something isn't allowed.

yourTurn.prompt: Say there's no need: *Hay que tener miedo.*
yourTurn.why: *No hay que* means there's no need to.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: You have to eat well. (as anyone does)
yourTurn.why: *Uno tiene que* gives a rule for people in general.

pitfalls.why: *No hay que* means you don't need to, so for a ban say *no se debe*.
Nothing goes between *se debe* and the infinitive.

personal: Tell us one rule that is true for everybody, using *hay que*, *uno tiene que* or *no se debe*.
